description: Tier 8 PR 1: Invert the architecture from poll-based scanning to event-driven supervision. The main brain becomes an open-trade supervisor that diagnoses close events, applies adaptive policy responses, and triggers the scanner on-demand via a slot/trigger model. Pure new files plus minimal wiring into continuous.py.

userStories.title: Create TradeSlot state machine and SlotManager
userStories.description: As the supervision core, I need an explicit state machine per pair so I can track where each pair is in the lifecycle and decide when to trigger scans.
acceptanceCriteria: File created at src/scanner/automation/trade_slots.py
TradeSlotState enum with states: IDLE, SCANNING, CANDIDATE, ARMED, OPEN, SUPERVISING, CLOSING, DIAGNOSING, ADAPTING, COOLDOWN

TradeSlot dataclass with fields: pair (str), state (TradeSlotState), entered_state_at (float, time.time()), trade_id (Optional[str]), metadata (dict, default_factory=dict), cooldown_until (Optional[float], default=None)
SlotManager class with __init__(max_concurrent: int = 3) maintaining a dict of pair -> TradeSlot

SlotManager.transition(pair, new_state, **metadata) validates legal transitions and updates entered_state_at. Raises ValueError on illegal transition. Legal transitions: IDLE->SCANNING, SCANNING->CANDIDATE, SCANNING->IDLE, CANDIDATE->ARMED, CANDIDATE->IDLE, ARMED->OPEN, ARMED->IDLE, OPEN->SUPERVISING, SUPERVISING->CLOSING, CLOSING->DIAGNOSING, DIAGNOSING->ADAPTING, ADAPTING->IDLE, ADAPTING->COOLDOWN, COOLDOWN->IDLE, any->IDLE (reset)
SlotManager.available_slots() returns count of pairs in IDLE state that are not in cooldown (cooldown_until is None or < time.time())
SlotManager.open_positions() returns list of TradeSlot where state is OPEN or SUPERVISING
SlotManager.get_state(pair) returns TradeSlotState for pair, defaults to IDLE
SlotManager.set_cooldown(pair, duration_seconds) transitions to COOLDOWN and sets cooldown_until
SlotManager.check_cooldowns() auto-transitions any COOLDOWN pairs where cooldown_until < time.time() back to IDLE, returns list of freed pairs
All state transitions logged via structlog with pair, old_state, new_state
Import succeeds: python -c "from src.scanner.automation.trade_slots import SlotManager, TradeSlotState"
py_compile passes
userStories.notes: This is the foundation — every other module references TradeSlotState. Keep it simple, no persistence needed yet. The max_concurrent parameter controls how many pairs can be in non-IDLE states simultaneously.

userStories.title: Create CloseDiagnosis dataclass and CloseDiagnostician
userStories.description: As the supervision core, I need structured close-event diagnosis so the adaptive policy engine can reason about WHY a trade closed, not just win/loss.
acceptanceCriteria: File created at src/scanner/automation/close_diagnostician.py
CloseReason enum: SL_HIT, TP_HIT, TRAILING_SL, MANUAL, TIMEOUT, DRAWDOWN_GUARDIAN, REGIME_CHANGE, BREAKEVEN

CloseDiagnosis dataclass with fields: trade_id (str), pair (str), direction (str), close_reason (CloseReason), entry_price (float), exit_price (float), realized_pl (float), pnl_pips (float), duration_minutes (float), regime_at_entry (str), regime_at_exit (str), regime_changed (bool), confidence_at_entry (float), agents_correct (List[str]), agents_wrong (List[str]), entry_still_valid_1h (Optional[bool]), market_moved_after_close_pips (Optional[float]), timestamp (str)
CloseDiagnostician class with diagnose(trade_outcome: dict) -> CloseDiagnosis that maps raw trade journal entries to structured diagnosis

CloseDiagnostician.diagnose() infers CloseReason from exit_reason string (maps 'sl_hit'->SL_HIT, 'tp_hit'->TP_HIT, 'trailing'->TRAILING_SL, 'timeout'->TIMEOUT, 'drawdown'->DRAWDOWN_GUARDIAN, etc., default MANUAL)
CloseDiagnostician.diagnose() sets regime_changed = (regime_at_entry != regime_at_exit) when both are available, defaults False
CloseDiagnostician.diagnose() splits agent_reasons string into agents_correct (those that agreed with winning direction) and agents_wrong (those that disagreed), using trade_won and direction fields
CloseDiagnostician.batch_diagnose(outcomes: List[dict]) -> List[CloseDiagnosis] for processing multiple closes
Import succeeds
py_compile passes
userStories.notes: The trade_outcome dict matches the schema in trained_data/trade_journal_rl.json entries. Key fields to expect: pair, direction, entry_price, exit_price, realized_pl, pnl_pips, exit_reason, confidence, regime, agent_reasons (comma-separated string), duration_minutes, trade_won (bool). If a field is missing, use sensible defaults. entry_still_valid_1h and market_moved_after_close_pips are left as None — they'll be populated by a future enrichment step.

userStories.title: Create AdaptivePolicy and SupervisionPolicyEngine
userStories.description: As the supervision core, I need time-decaying policy overrides so the system can dynamically tighten gates, pause pairs, or adjust sizing based on recent close diagnoses — not just nudge RL weights. IMPORTANT: This is SEPARATE from the Tier 7 PolicyEngine (action gating). This handles adaptive supervision responses.
acceptanceCriteria: File created at src/scanner/automation/supervision_policy_engine.py
PolicyType enum: PAIR_COOLDOWN, GATE_TIGHTEN, GATE_LOOSEN, SIZING_ADJUST, REGIME_OVERRIDE, ENTRY_BLOCK

AdaptivePolicy dataclass with fields: policy_id (str, uuid4), policy_type (PolicyType), pair (Optional[str], None=global), parameter (str, e.g. 'min_confidence'), adjustment (float, e.g. +0.10), reason (str), created_at (float, time.time()), expires_at (float), source_diagnosis_ids (List[str])
SupervisionPolicyEngine class with __init__() maintaining a list of active policies
SupervisionPolicyEngine.add_policy(policy) appends to active list, logs via structlog
SupervisionPolicyEngine.get_active_policies(pair=None, policy_type=None) returns list of non-expired policies, optionally filtered by pair and/or type

SupervisionPolicyEngine.get_effective_adjustment(pair, parameter) returns the sum of all active policy adjustments for that pair+parameter combo (including global policies where pair is None), returns 0.0 if no active policies
SupervisionPolicyEngine.expire_stale() removes policies where time.time() > expires_at, returns count removed
SupervisionPolicyEngine.has_active_block(pair) returns True if any ENTRY_BLOCK or PAIR_COOLDOWN policy is active for that pair
SupervisionPolicyEngine.to_dict() serializes active policies for dashboard/logging
SupervisionPolicyEngine.clear() removes all policies
All policy additions and expirations logged via structlog
Import succeeds: python -c "from src.scanner.automation.supervision_policy_engine import SupervisionPolicyEngine, AdaptivePolicy, PolicyType"
py_compile passes
userStories.notes: NAMING: This is SupervisionPolicyEngine in supervision_policy_engine.py — NOT the Tier 7 PolicyEngine in policy_engine.py. The Tier 7 one gates actions (allow/deny). This one manages time-decaying adaptive overrides (cooldowns, gate tightening). They are separate concerns. Policies are intentionally ephemeral — they live in memory and expire. No disk persistence needed. The adjustment field is additive: if min_confidence is 0.55 and a policy adds +0.10, the effective threshold becomes 0.65. Multiple policies can stack.

userStories.title: Create ScanTrigger and TriggerRegistry
userStories.description: As the supervision core, I need a registry of conditions that trigger scanner runs so scans happen on meaningful events rather than a dumb 5-minute clock.
acceptanceCriteria: File created at src/scanner/automation/trigger_registry.py
TriggerType enum: SLOT_OPENED, REGIME_TRANSITION, SESSION_OPEN, VOLATILITY_SPIKE, SCHEDULED_SWEEP, MANUAL, COOLDOWN_EXPIRED

ScanTrigger dataclass with fields: trigger_type (TriggerType), pairs (Optional[List[str]], None=all pairs), constraints (dict, default_factory=dict, e.g. {'exclude_pattern': 'mean_reversion'}), priority (int, default=5), timestamp (float, default_factory=time.time), source (str, default='system')
TriggerRegistry class with __init__(sweep_interval_minutes: float = 30.0)
TriggerRegistry.fire(trigger: ScanTrigger) appends trigger to pending queue (collections.deque, maxlen=100)
TriggerRegistry.drain() returns list of all pending triggers and clears the queue
TriggerRegistry.has_pending() returns bool
TriggerRegistry.schedule_sweep(pairs: Optional[List[str]] = None) creates a SCHEDULED_SWEEP trigger with given pairs
TriggerRegistry.should_sweep() returns True if sweep_interval_minutes has elapsed since last sweep, resets timer
All trigger fires logged via structlog with trigger_type, pairs count, source
Import succeeds
py_compile passes
userStories.notes: The TriggerRegistry is a lightweight queue — triggers go in, the SupervisionCore drains them. The constraints dict is open-ended: the scanner will interpret it. The sweep_interval_minutes is the fallback polling interval (30 min default, much less aggressive than 5 min). Pairs=None means scan all configured pairs.

userStories.title: Create SupervisionCore — the main brain
userStories.description: As the system, I need a supervision core that watches open positions, processes close events through the diagnostician, applies adaptive policies, and fires scan triggers — replacing the scan-first loop with a supervise-first loop.
acceptanceCriteria: File created at src/scanner/automation/supervision_core.py

SupervisionCore class with __init__(slot_manager: SlotManager, diagnostician: CloseDiagnostician, policy_engine: SupervisionPolicyEngine, trigger_registry: TriggerRegistry, config: Optional[dict] = None)

SupervisionCore stores config with defaults: {'max_concurrent': 3, 'cooldown_seconds': 3600, 'consecutive_loss_cooldown': 2, 'supervision_tiers': {15: 'tick', 120: '1m', 480: '5m'}, 'sweep_interval_minutes': 30.0}

SupervisionCore.process_close_event(trade_outcome: dict) -> CloseDiagnosis: runs diagnostician.diagnose(), transitions slot to DIAGNOSING then ADAPTING, calls _apply_adaptive_response(), transitions slot to IDLE or COOLDOWN, fires SLOT_OPENED trigger if slot freed, returns diagnosis

SupervisionCore._apply_adaptive_response(diagnosis: CloseDiagnosis): if consecutive losses >= consecutive_loss_cooldown for same pair, adds PAIR_COOLDOWN policy with cooldown_seconds duration. If diagnosis.regime_changed and not trade_won, adds GATE_TIGHTEN policy (+0.05 to min_confidence) for 2 hours. If trade_won and diagnosis.close_reason == TP_HIT and duration_minutes < 30, adds SIZING_ADJUST policy (+0.1 to atr_tp_multiplier) for 4 hours
SupervisionCore._consecutive_losses dict tracks consecutive loss count per pair, resets on win
SupervisionCore.get_supervision_interval(trade_age_minutes: float) -> str returns the check frequency string from supervision_tiers based on trade age

SupervisionCore.tick() calls policy_engine.expire_stale(), slot_manager.check_cooldowns() (fires COOLDOWN_EXPIRED triggers for freed pairs), and trigger_registry.should_sweep() (fires SCHEDULED_SWEEP if due)
SupervisionCore.get_status() -> dict returns: open_positions count, available_slots, active_policies count, pending_triggers count, consecutive_losses dict
Import succeeds
py_compile passes
userStories.notes: SupervisionCore does NOT run its own thread or loop — it exposes tick() and process_close_event() which the continuous.py loop calls. This keeps it testable and avoids threading issues. The supervision_tiers config maps trade age (minutes) to check frequency labels — the caller interprets these. _apply_adaptive_response is deliberately simple in this PR: 3 rules. Future PRs will add more sophisticated responses.
